headlines.summary: Follow CNBC's 2026 Workforce Executive Summit for live updates on Walmart's AI strategy, changing job skills, hiring, employee benefits and the future of work.
headlines.article_text: CNBC Workforce Executive Summit 2026 live updates: AI at work Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Mikkelwilliam | E+ | Getty Images Today's workplace faces a litany of challenges. Whether it's shifting power dynamics between employers and employees, the accelerating impact of artificial intelligence on how we work and the skills we need, or the financial stresses that employees of all ranks are feeling, these issues and more are challenging the cohesion of workplace communities. To address these issues, CNBC is convening its premiere council of human resource executives in New York City on Tuesday for the annual CNBC Workforce Executive Summit. The event is exclusive to members of CNBC's Workforce Executive Council. For more about the WEC and to apply for membership, visit www.cnbccouncils.com/wec . 2 Min Ago Digital transformation is “two of the worst words ever used in the history of work” – former LinkedIn CHRO Steve Cadigan When Steve Cadigan was LinkedIn's chief human resources officer, he told CNBC's Leslie Picker at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit that a common trope at the networking platform was that whenever another company announced it was going through a digital transformation, that meant job cuts were on the horizon. "Let's look at all the people in the company that just announced a digital transformation and see who's looking for a new job," Cadigan told Picker. "When you tell employees we're going through a digital transformation, you're basically saying, 'Well, we care about the technology, not about you.'" While companies have heavily invested in AI tools, Cadigan said many have not "built the trust to get people to the point where they can say, 'Yeah, just go ahead and reinvent your job; we got your back.'" As more companies signal AI-driven job cuts, Cadigan said many employees see the first implementation of AI as "cutting people in the name of AI." Instead, Cadigan stressed that organizations need to promise to workers that they are investing in their growth and development, and that while they can't predict how AI will change their jobs or their future employment, these companies will "grow and develop you … we're going to make you a better human being and a better professional, and if things don't work out here, you're going to be a better person on the other side." "That's a bigger promise," he said. — Ian Thomas 30 Min Ago The CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit is underway! The entrance of the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City on October 27, 2026. CNBC The programming has kicked off here in New York: first up is Steve Cadigan, the creator and author of the Human Advantage Framework, a research-informed framework for understanding, assessing, and developing the human capabilities that matter most in the age of AI. Cadigan will be speaking with CNBC's Leslie Picker about how AI is reshaping work and how employers need to equip employees to adapt to this fast rate of change. 1 Hour Ago Health insurance costs are growing, with no end in sight watch now VIDEO 10:03 10:03 Rising costs of health benefits: Total cost per employee expected to rise 8.2% in 2027 Squawk Box Most Americans under age 65 — about 166 million people — get health insurance via employer-sponsored health plans. That is generally subsided by their employers, who cover a large portion of the monthly premium payments workers pay. The average worker paid $6,850 of annual premiums in 2025, while employers contributed more than $20,000 per worker, according to KFF. In 2027, the cost for employers to provide health benefits will rise by an estimated 8.2% per worker, on average. That represents the largest increase since 2003, even with additional cost-reduction measures by employers, according to Marsh. Aon, another consulting firm, expects employer costs to jump 9.5% in 2027 — the fourth consecutive year of "elevated" healthcare costs, "extending one of the most sustained periods of health care inflation employers have faced in decades," the firm said in a press release in August. Growth in the cost of deductibles and family premiums has each outpaced inflation over the past decade , rising 54% and 53%, respectively, versus an overall inflation rate of 36%, according to KFF. All of those cost increases are likely leading to cuts in benefits next year for workers who are covered by plans from their jobs: Nearly 6 out of 10 employers — 59% — plan to make cost-cutting changes to health benefits in 2027, including by adding higher deductibles, according to Marsh. It polled more than 1,800 employers from June 10 to August 10. HealthEquity CFO James Lucania will be speaking later today at the CNBC Workforce Summit about how CHROs and benefits managers can use AI to streamline healthcare costs, and at the same time, make out-of-pocket payments easier for employees to understand and manage, all while helping each of them get the care they need. 1 Hour Ago AI is fueling uncertainty in the job market A sign on the Microsoft campus in Redmond, Washington, US, Oct. 26, 2026. David Ryder | Reuters There are many forces changing the workplace. But few are having the impact that AI is, shifting roles and job expectations, as well as headcount. Microsoft announced this week that it is offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees, a measure that comes as the company strives to balance a costly AI build-out with efficiency. The software company has been ramping up its spending on data centers to accommodate high AI computing demand as it supplies cloud services to a number of AI companies. The offer follows a voluntary retirement program announced at Microsoft this past spring and 4,800 jobs cut in July. American Express said last week that it would be cutting thousands of employees as the leading credit card company prepares for artificial intelligence to take over more of its internal processes. Amex is eliminating 5% of its global workforce and taking a $336 million restructuring charge, CEO Stephen Squeri told analysts Friday on the company's third-quarter earnings call. The firm had almost 77,000 employees at the end of 2025. Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec told CNBC in an interview that the restructuring was to make American Express "leaner, more agile, and also to prepare for AI." "You don't want to automate processes that are not optimally structured," Le Caillec said. "So what we're doing here is to reduce layers and increase spans of controls, so that we can automate and take advantage of AI in the coming quarters and the coming years." The Amex announcement reflects a broader trend across financial services, where banks are working to replace repetitive roles with AI automation. On Thursday, Barclays confirmed plans to trim 5,000 jobs — also roughly 5% of its staff — in another tech-driven cost initiative. The moves come even as the sector is enjoying robust profits from growing consumer spending and resilient credit. Skydance also announced voluntary buyouts following its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, a step driven largely by the consolidation, but it also comes as executives acknowledge that AI will transform the company. In addition, Qualcomm cut jobs earlier this month as the company pivots towards AI data centers and non-smartphone markets. - Colleen McKown 2 Hours Ago What role do cities play in AI oversight? watch now VIDEO 4:51 04:51 NYC council speaker: Need for regulation was big takeaway from NYC AI hearing The Exchange Earlier this month, the New York City Council held a legislative investigation concerning artificial intelligence safety risks, with senior leaders from Anthropic , OpenAI, Google and Meta testifying under oath about the potential dangers of the technology and outlined current safety measures. headlines.article_text: Oracle integrates ChatGPT, Codex into apps, expands cloud chip lineup Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Oracle is adding OpenAI's ChatGPT and Codex to its application stack, extending enterprise access to OpenAI tools. Oracle said OCI will add Google TPUs, OpenAI's Jalapeño chip and Cerebras hardware as customers seek more silicon options. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is set to join Oracle co-CEO Clay Magouyrk for a keynote at Oracle AI World. In this article OPENAI.FG CBRS ORCL GOOGL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Oracle on Tuesday announced an expanded collaboration with OpenAI that brings the artificial intelligence lab's ChatGPT and Codex into the software maker's applications to make databases more actionable. Mahesh Thiagarajan, Oracle's president of Cloud Infrastructure, told CNBC at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas that using ChatGPT "allows anybody to build an application, deploy it, manage it." OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is set to join Oracle co-CEO Clay Magouyrk on stage for an Oracle AI World keynote on Tuesday at 12:40 p.m. ET. For OpenAI, the announcement represents another example of the frontier lab's push into the enterprise market, just one day after its key competitor, Anthropic , filed its S-1 as it heads toward an initial public offering . Oracle's database plays a crucial role in underpinning businesses across healthcare and finance in logging and securing data. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman speaking at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas on Oct. 27th, 2026. CNBC Thiagarajan said his team observed OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model get trained at Oracle's Stargate data center campus in Abilene, Texas, and could see the real-time benefits. "More businesses are choosing OpenAI as we make it easier to put AI to work through the tools and systems they already use," said Greg Brockman, president and co-founder of OpenAI, in the press release. Oracle also said Tuesday that it is making different hardware accessible on its cloud infrastructure, including Google 's tensor processing unit AI chips and OpenAI's Jalapeño chip. "Now customers can actually have infinite possibilities in terms of how they can drive AI," Thiagarajan said. It is the first time Google's custom chips will run on another hyperscaler's cloud, and illustrates how the companies are increasingly looking for opportunities to get their hardware in the hands of the frontier labs. Thiagarajan added that the scarcity of chips remains an ongoing issue and that customers like OpenAI can benefit from having different accelerators to choose from. When asked whether this marks a pivot away from Nvidia GPUs, Thiagarajan said no, adding that Nvidia chips are "the best, most fungible," and that the AI market remains incredibly large. OpenAI's Jalapeno chip and Cerebras will also run on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. The Cerebras deal is material, but the AI chipmaker won't be disclosing the scale because it's in a quiet period, a Cerebras spokesperson said. Cerebras stock climbed about 8% following the news. Oracle shares were up nearly 5% on Tuesday. Read more CNBC tech news A guide to some of the biggest risks in Anthropic's IPO prospectus Nvidia, AMD to invest $4 billion in Meta as tech giants deepen AI partnership Apple responds to user reports of broken iPhone Duo screens on new foldable phone Anthropic's IPO plans: 900% revenue retention, but $80 billion in first-half losses The announcement comes seven months after market-leading cloud Amazon Web Services announced plans to bring Cerebras hardware into its data centers , a major point of validation. Thiagarajan also addressed Oracle's multibillion New Mexico data center dubbed Project Jupiter and the ongoing pushback it's receiving from the local community. He said Jupiter represents just one of the 30-40 different data center projects in development, per quarter, for the company. "We're actually not too worried about what we're doing because I think we're building global infrastructure," he said. A hearing to address air quality permitting is scheduled for Dec. 7 in Sunland Park, where the controversial data center has already broken ground. The political pushback tied to the project prompted Oracle to deliver a force majeure notice to its backer Blue Owl Capital last month. Right now, Oracle maintains that the project is on schedule. Investors are now counting down to Oracle's investor day, where investors will want to see if the company can back its fiscal year 2030 revenue targets and if the margin profile of its cloud deals has changed due to the rising cost of capital. Bank of America analysts wrote to clients that updates on Oracle's major data center projects are among the topics they expect clarity on at the meeting. Oracle shares are down more than 30% this year due in part to concerns about how the company plans to finance its ambitious digital infrastructure pipeline. —CNBC's Jordan Novet contributed to this article Oracle stock chart. watch now VIDEO 10:36 10:36 Watch the full discussion between OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Oracle co-CEO Clay Magouyrk News Videos Choose CNBC as your preferred source on Google and never miss a moment from the most trusted name in business news.

headlines.article_text: Ripple strikes deal with Robinhood to expand its RLUSD digital dollar Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Ripple has struck a deal with Robinhood to expand the use of Ripple's digital dollar, RLUSD, broadening trading and financing options for institutional clients and improving Robinhood's internal money management. The partnership meets Robinhood's ambition of becoming a global financial superapp, centralizing more of its customers' financial lives while expanding the underlying infrastructure that can serve both retail and institutional clients. As the crypto industry evolves beyond trading and markets shift to 24/7 liquidity, stablecoins are becoming essential financial infrastructure. In this article HOOD Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Ripple and Robinhood Getty Images Ripple has struck a deal with Robinhood to expand the reach of its digital dollar, RLUSD , strengthening trading and financing links between their institutional businesses and improving Robinhood's internal money management. The partnership involves using RLUSD to settle institutional trades, automate Robinhood's treasury operations and expand access to digital asset trading and financing through Ripple Prime and Bitstamp, the global crypto exchange acquired by Robinhood last year . It also helps meet Robinhood's ambition of becoming a global financial superapp, centralizing its customers' financial lives while expanding the underlying infrastructure that can serve both retail and institutional clients. "Utility is what moves stablecoins forward. Working with Ripple, Bitstamp and Robinhood will have access to RLUSD for institutional settlement, Ripple Treasury for our operations and Ripple Prime for financing," Robinhood Crypto General Manager Johann Kerbrat said in a statement shared with CNBC. "That is what a connected, global financial system looks like." Workhorse Stablecoins have long been a workhorse of the crypto world, giving traders a way to move money among exchanges, buy and sell crypto assets, and park funds between trades without having to convert back into traditional currency. But as the crypto industry evolves beyond trading and markets move toward 24/7 liquidity, stablecoins are becoming essential financial infrastructure because of their ability to enable near-instant settlement and move dollar-denominated value at any time, regardless of traditional banking hours. As firms look to do more with stablecoins beyond simply listing them on exchanges, stablecoin issuers are betting they'll favor a one-stop-shop approach that bundles the technology and services needed to move money, settle trades and manage cash. "Stablecoins have evolved from a crypto trading tool into a critical piece of financial infrastructure," Ripple President Monica Long told CNBC. "The clearest evidence of this is where they're now being embedded — from corporate payments to capital markets. Our partnership with Robinhood reflects that evolution." "This is about much more than trading," she added. "It's about fundamentally changing how money moves and is managed — giving institutions the ability to operate 24/7/365, unlocking liquidity and putting capital to work more efficiently." Circle Internet Group, a Ripple competitor, is positioning itself for a similar future, where winning platforms, in addition to issuing stablecoins, also provide the infrastructure to put them to work. Earlier this year, for example, it launched the Circle Payments Network, connecting financial institutions and payment providers using its flagship USDC stablecoin and other digital assets for cross-border payments. The network is Circle's answer to the 8-year-old Ripple Payments business, a service that helps businesses move money across borders, using any of several assets moving through that system, including USDC, Ripple-created XRP and, as of its debut in December 2024, RLUSD. RLUSD's market cap has grown to more than $2.5 billion . Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC still dominate the total stablecoin market, which now exceeds $300 billion . RLUSD will also be listed on Robinhood's trading platform, and is currently available to traders on Bitstamp as well as Robinhood Chain, the company's home-grown blockchain for tokenized stocks and other assets. Robinhood, which reports third-quarter results for the three months ended in September after the market closes, rose about 2.5% in early trading Tuesday, snapping a three-day decline.
